GitHub comes into the app: CI, Actions, and getting repositories in and out.

### CI status everywhere

- **History** shows ✓ / ✗ / ● beside each commit, from one batched request for the rows on screen; running checks refresh every 30 s.
- **Actions view (⌘5)**: workflow runs (all, this branch, failed), their jobs, and each job's log split into steps, with the failing step opened and the error lines highlighted. **Re-run failed jobs**, **Re-run all**, **Re-run job** and **Cancel**. Runs in progress refresh every 10 s.

### Repositories in and out of GitHub

- **Clone from GitHub**: pick from your and your organisations' repositories (newest first, private and forks marked), filter, or paste `owner/name` or a URL.
- **Publish to GitHub**: a repository without a remote gets a _Publish to GitHub…_ entry in the sidebar; choose owner, name, description and visibility, and it is created and pushed.
- **Fork on GitHub** from the ⌘K palette: your fork becomes `origin`, the original stays as `upstream`.

### Open on GitHub

- Right-click a commit, a changed file, a branch or a tag to open it on GitHub, copy a permalink, or copy its SHA, path or name, next to the usual check out / branch / cherry-pick / revert.

### Also

- The repository given on the command line, or the last one, now opens reliably on launch.
- Everything is in English and 简体中文.

### Install

Download the file for your system below. The builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet: on macOS right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time (or run `xattr -cr "/Applications/Git Graph.app"`); on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**. Pull requests and Actions use the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) sign-in (`gh auth login`).
